note: Independent ski areas not on the Indy Pass (checked against indyskipass.com/our-resorts on 2026-10-26).

prospects.name: Boyce Park Ski Area
prospects.ownership: Allegheny County (county park)
prospects.fit_notes: County-run community hill (two chairlifts, tubing, terrain parks, lessons) sold through online registration links on the county site; a government operator with no dedicated ski-ops tech stack is a natural fit for an all-in-one platform and the standalone patrol module.

prospects.name: Mystic Mountain at Nemacolin
prospects.ownership: Part of Nemacolin resort (single-property resort owner; owner not confirmed)
prospects.fit_notes: Small amenity ski hill inside a luxury resort; reportedly restricted to overnight guests and members since 2021-22 and open mostly Fri-Sun, so a weaker fit (the patrol module alone is the likely angle).

prospects.name: Holiday Valley Resort
prospects.ownership: Win-Sum Ski Corp (independent corporation with local board; calls itself an independent resort)

contacts.name: Bonnie Koschir
contacts.title: Chair, Win-Sum Ski Corp Board of Directors

contacts.name: Kate Rauber
contacts.title: Vice President of Skier Services; Secretary, Win-Sum Ski Corp

prospects.fit_notes: Largest independent in western NY, with a year-round business (golf, adventure park, coaster) and a leadership team reshuffled in Feb 2026. It sits at the top of the size range (13 lifts), so it's a bigger-ticket full-platform deal.

prospects.name: HoliMont
prospects.ownership: Private members-only ski club (founded by William Merk; structure not confirmed)
prospects.fit_notes: Described as North America's largest private ski club. It's investing about $1M (2025) in snowmaking, electrical, and cats with IDA tax breaks, and its member billing and access needs differ from a public mountain. It also runs a bike park in summer.

prospects.name: Kissing Bridge
prospects.ownership: Kissing Bridge All Seasons Resort Inc. (Rhett McNulty, California tech investor; bought Nov 2024)

contacts.name: Matt Thomas
contacts.title: General Manager (hired March 2026; ex-Telluride risk management director, ex-Roundtop VP/GM)

prospects.fit_notes: Top prospect: a tech-investor owner since late 2024 who publicly plans technology investments and a four-season operation, plus a new GM (March 2026) with a risk-management/patrol background who should value a deep patrol module. It's also expanding snowmaking and summer biking.

prospects.name: Bristol Mountain
prospects.ownership: Independent, family-run (founded by Fred Sarkis 1964; GM Dan Fuller); current owner entity not confirmed
prospects.fit_notes: Biggest vertical between the Catskills and the Rockies, with ski school, rentals, retail shop, race programs, and summer aerial adventure park/zip lines, so lots of modules apply. Long-tenured independent management.

prospects.name: Windham Mountain Club
prospects.ownership: Private investor group (majority: Beall Investment Partners and Kemmons Wilson Hospitality Partners since April 2023)

contacts.name: Kristen Leach
contacts.title: President (promoted from Director of Membership, April 2025)

contacts.name: Ian Peters
contacts.title: Vice President of Operations (formerly Director of Technology)

prospects.fit_notes: Semi-private membership club since 2023 that dropped Ikon for 2025-26; the new VP Ops came up through technology. Membership/access control plus public ticketing is a strong angle, though at 1,600 ft and 11 lifts it's near the size ceiling.

prospects.name: Toggenburg Mountain
prospects.ownership: Wheeler family of Countryside Excavation (local; bought Oct 2026 after NY AG antitrust win against prior owner Intermountain)

contacts.name: James Wheeler
contacts.title: Owner, Countryside Excavation (lead of new ownership group; another outlet names Douglas Wheeler)

prospects.fit_notes: Greenfield opportunity: closed since 2021, new local owners plan to rebuild and reopen for 2027-28 with no legacy systems. Owner asked the public not to call, so approach later via a formal channel.

prospects.name: Campgaw Mountain Ski Area
prospects.ownership: Bergen County park (Campgaw Mountain Reservation); ski operator entity not confirmed
prospects.fit_notes: Small, busy NYC-metro learning hill with lessons, adaptive program, rentals, night skiing, and a large tubing park. It has a ski patrol page and uses a third-party e-commerce vendor that could be displaced.

prospects.name: Wachusett Mountain
prospects.ownership: Crowley family (Wachusett Mountain Associates; operates on state DCR reservation under lease)
prospects.fit_notes: High-volume family-owned day area near Boston with heavy night skiing and ski-club traffic. It just put in a ~$20M six-pack (2025-26), so it's investing in capacity and crowd management.

prospects.name: Nashoba Valley Ski Area
prospects.ownership: Fletcher family (founded by Al Fletcher 1964; run by Al Jr. and Pam Fletcher per 2015 report)

contacts.name: Al Fletcher Jr.
contacts.title: Co-operator, family business (source from 2015, check current)

contacts.name: Pam Fletcher
contacts.title: Co-operator, family business (source from 2015, check current)

prospects.fit_notes: Family-owned suburban learning hill with a big lesson program (Pre-K through adaptive), rentals, night skiing, and New England's largest tubing park, which means high transaction volume on a small footprint.

prospects.name: Ski Ward
prospects.ownership: LaCroix family (Ski Ward, Inc., since 1990; land leased from Ward family)
prospects.fit_notes: Tiny family-owned hill with heavy school-team racing, summer snow/tubing ops, and a 2025-26 opening on Oct 18. Small staff is a good match for a simple all-in-one or patrol-only plan.

prospects.name: Yawgoo Valley Ski Area
prospects.ownership: de Wardener family (owned since 1980)

contacts.name: Patti Davis
contacts.title: Director of the Snow Sports School

prospects.fit_notes: Rhode Island's only ski area, family-run, with 95 instructors, about 1,200 students a week, and a 900-name lesson waitlist run by lottery. That is a clear pain point for ski-school scheduling and registration. It also has a summer water park.

prospects.name: Mount Southington Ski Area
prospects.ownership: Independent private ownership (founded by Richman family/investors; current owner not confirmed)
prospects.fit_notes: Fully lit night-skiing day area in central CT that keeps reinvesting (new Partek chairs 2021-22 and 2023-24). It's independent and small, so a good full-platform candidate; GM name not found.

prospects.name: Gunstock Mountain Resort
prospects.ownership: Belknap County (overseen by the Gunstock Area Commission)

contacts.name: Robert Drake
contacts.title: President and General Manager (started Aug 2024; ex-Middlebury Snowbowl, Bridger Bowl)

contacts.name: Doug Lambert
contacts.title: Chair, Gunstock Area Commission (as of July 2024)

prospects.fit_notes: County-owned with public procurement and governance scrutiny after the 2022 management walkout; a GM since 2024 who comes from community/nonprofit areas. It runs year-round (coaster, summer park).

prospects.name: Cochran's Ski Area
prospects.ownership: Nonprofit (Cochran's Ski Area, Inc., 501(c)(3)); Cochran family remains involved

contacts.name: Jimmy Cochran
contacts.title: Runs the ski area (formal title not published)

prospects.fit_notes: Tiny donor-funded nonprofit hill ($19 weekend ticket), with surface lifts, night lights, and race programs. It's price-sensitive, so the $149/month patrol module or a lightweight plan is the realistic sale.

prospects.name: Snow Trails
prospects.ownership: family-owned (Carto family); privately owned, same management since inception
prospects.fit_notes: Ohio's only family-owned winter resort, not on Indy, and investing steadily (new rope tow, SMI guns, PistenBully, rental fleet refresh for 2025-26). Mid-size operation with ski school, rental center, tubing and night skiing, all of which a single platform could unify.

prospects.name: Welch Village
prospects.ownership: family-owned (Nelson family); operated by Peter Zotalis, grandson of late owner Leigh Nelson

contacts.name: Peter Zotalis
contacts.title: Operator (grandson of late owner Leigh Nelson) (source from 2023, check current)

prospects.fit_notes: Third-generation family area that just added a new quad for 2025-26, large lesson/camp/race programs, and runs on accesso, so a displacement play. Generational ownership transition after the founder's 2023 death is a natural moment to re-evaluate systems.

prospects.name: Buck Hill
prospects.ownership: privately owned (David and Corrine Solner; Don McClure was a co-buyer in 2015)

contacts.name: Don McClure
contacts.title: General Manager and co-owner (source from 2015, check current)

prospects.fit_notes: Suburban Twin Cities hill with a large volunteer NSP patrol (80+ members, own website), heavy race and lesson programs, tubing and summer biking. A volunteer patrol of that size is a strong fit for the $149/month patrol module.

prospects.name: Wild Mountain
prospects.ownership: family-owned (Larsen family)

contacts.name: Nathan Hakseth
contacts.title: General Manager (also oversees Snowsports School and Competitions)

prospects.fit_notes: Family-owned, year-round business (ski area plus summer waterpark) with a GM promoted in 2024 from ski school, so lessons and staff scheduling are close to his heart. Recent lift and base-area investment shows willingness to spend.

prospects.name: Cannonsburg Ski Area
prospects.ownership: privately owned and operated (owner not named in sources); same operators bought Pando Winter Sports Park in 2015

contacts.name: Matt Chapman
contacts.title: Ski Patrol Director (source from 2022, check current)

prospects.fit_notes: Busy Grand Rapids-area hill with the state's largest tubing facility, multiple parks, junior academy and real summer program (bike team, disc golf). Kent County tried to buy it in 2023, so ownership/strategy may be in flux.

prospects.name: Mt. Holly
prospects.ownership: privately owned; current owner not identified in sources (not Vail, which owns nearby Mt. Brighton)
prospects.fit_notes: Detroit-area learn-to-ski hub (70th season in 2025-26) with heavy school/student patch programs and night operations, so ski school and staff scheduling volume is high. Long-tenured GM; ownership should be confirmed before outreach.

prospects.name: Bittersweet Ski Resort
prospects.ownership: family-owned (family not named in sources)
prospects.fit_notes: Family-owned southwest Michigan hill where lift tickets are reportedly sold on-site only, a clear gap for online ticketing and passes. GM in his third season as of late 2024 after several tough winters, so efficiency gains matter.

prospects.name: Timber Ridge Ski Area
prospects.ownership: family-owned (operating since 1961; family not named in sources)
prospects.fit_notes: Small family-owned Kalamazoo-area hill with night skiing, tubing and lessons sold through local parks departments. Classic community hill with a small staff that would benefit from an all-in-one system.

prospects.name: Snow Snake Ski & Golf
prospects.ownership: family-owned (Brockway family since 1957)
prospects.fit_notes: Small family hill with a 30+ PSIA/AASI instructor staff, sizable rental fleet and a four-lane tubing park, plus summer golf. Lots of moving parts for a small team.

prospects.name: Seven Oaks Recreation
prospects.ownership: family-owned (Bryan family; owner Joel Bryan)
prospects.fit_notes: Owner-operated central Iowa hill investing in snowmaking (23 guns, new ones added 2024) and running night skiing, tubing and lessons. Owner is the decision-maker, so the sales cycle should be short.

prospects.name: Crescent Hill at Hitchcock (formerly Mt. Crescent Ski Area)

contacts.name: Chris Andrew
contacts.title: Site Manager, Crescent Hill at Hitchcock

contacts.name: Mark Shoemaker

prospects.fit_notes: County-run hill near Omaha, recently rebranded, with its own ski patrol and online rental reservations; government owners value auditable patrol/incident records. Public procurement may mean an RFP, but budgets and decision-makers are visible.

prospects.name: Alpine Valley Resort
prospects.ownership: Wisconsin Resorts, Inc. (privately held; no other ski areas found)
prospects.fit_notes: Independent ski-in/ski-out resort with on-slope lodging and golf, in the Chicago/Milwaukee market next to Vail's Wilmot. Larger lift count (12) is at the upper end of the size range; hotel plus ski ops makes it a bigger multi-module deal.

prospects.name: Hanson Hills Recreation Area
prospects.ownership: nonprofit Grayling Recreation Authority (consortium of Grayling Township, Crawford County, Crawford AuSable Schools and at-large members); land under State Military Board
prospects.fit_notes: Nonprofit, government-consortium community hill (Michigan's first downhill area, 1929) with very small staff and volunteer roots. A natural fit for the standalone $149/month patrol module or a lightweight all-in-one.

prospects.name: Otsego Resort (Otsego Club)
prospects.ownership: Osprey Recreational Properties (bought 2007; golf/resort company, no other ski areas found; current ownership should be confirmed)

contacts.name: Jeff Morrison
contacts.title: Director of Ski Operations (source from 2015, check current)

prospects.fit_notes: Historic (1939) former private ski club turned public resort with lodging and two golf courses; mixes members, resort guests and day skiers. Contacts are dated, so verify leadership first.

prospects.name: Mt. Zion Recreational Complex
prospects.ownership: Gogebic Community College (college ski hill, home of its Ski Area Management program)
prospects.fit_notes: College-owned hill that trains future ski area managers through the SAM program; the long-time manager/SAM director retired Oct 2023 and no successor was found. No online ticket purchase on its page, and a reference customer here would put Verdynt/OS in front of future industry managers.

prospects.fit_notes: Community nonprofit (~600 staff, ~$20M revenue) with serious avalanche terrain and an early 2026 closure that put pressure on budgets; bigger vertical than the target but only 8 lifts, and patrol is a natural wedge.
